title: Tenant credit resurfacer and usage zoning validator
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
We need a background job ("Tenant Credit Resurfacer") and a companion validator that examines per-tenant usage zoning to detect and correct drift between real-time metered events and the canonical billing ledger. This ticket covers design and implementation of both: an idempotent resurface worker that can re-emit or repair missing credit allocations for tenants (bounded to a lookback window), and a validator that flags usage-zone mismatches (region, capacity tier, model variant) that can cause improper routing of charges.

Background & motivation:
- We periodically observe small but persistent discrepancies between streaming meter events (edge ingestion) and the consolidated billing ledger. Causes include late-arriving events, cross-region routing changes, and transient multi-model route splits. These discrepancies sometimes lead to incorrect tenant credits or double-charging when a retroactive correction job runs.
- Existing reconciliation jobs focus on ledger-level aggregates. We need a finer-grained approach that: (1) repairs tenant-level credit states without causing duplicate credits; and (2) validates that per-request zoning attributes (region, route, model_variant, capacity_tier) used by the billing policy align with the ledger attribution, surfacing anomalies for manual review or automated corrective actions.

Goals:
- Implement an idempotent resurfacer that can safely replay and emit missing tenant credit transactions for a configurable lookback window (default 7 days).
- Build a zoning validator that compares ingestion attributes to ledger attribution and produces a confidence score + anomaly reasons for each mismatch.
- Prevent duplicate credits by using a deterministic dedupe key and ledger-level preflight checks.
- Expose dashboards and alerts for high anomaly rates (>0.1% of events or >5 tenants affected in 24h).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not replace the existing nightly ledger consolidator. It augments it with targeted repair logic and a validator pipeline.

Design notes:
- Input sources: streaming-meter-events (Kafka topic meter.events.enriched), canonical-ledger (materialized view ledger.transactions_partitioned_by_day), and per-tenant routing history (tenant-routing-log).
- Resurfacer algorithm: iterate tenants in the lookback window -> compute expected credit deltas by replaying meter.events with the same billing policy -> check ledger for matching credit transactions using dedupe_key = sha256(tenant_id + event_hash + billing_policy_version + time_bucket) -> if missing, emit corrective credit transaction to the ledger-ingest topic with metadata {source: "resurfacer", original_event_time, repair_window_origin}.
- Validator algorithm: stream-join incoming events with latest ledger attribution and tenant-routing-log; compute zoning_diff = set(req_attrs) \u2260 set(ledger_attrs) and generate anomaly records with reason tags (late_arrival, multi_route_conflict, region_mismatch, model_variant_fallback).
- Idempotency & safety: all resurfacer-emitted corrections must be annotated and require ledger write-side preflight that rejects duplicates by dedupe_key. Corrections must be reversible via a compensating transaction if a downstream post-check discovers an over-credit.

Acceptance criteria:
- The resurfacer can run end-to-end in staging and repair simulated missing credits without creating duplicates in 1000 synthetic tenant tests.
- The validator produces anomaly records with at least 90% precision on a labelled test set (created from three weeks of historical incidents).
- Dashboards added: resurfacer-run-summary (repairs emitted, rejected-by-preflight, duration), validator-anomaly-rate (per-tenant, per-region), and a top-10 reasons heatmap.
- Pager and slack alerts created for sustained high anomaly rates and resurfacer error rates.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (Spike, 3 days): prototype resurfacer logic in Python batch worker reading from the materialized ledger view and meter event S3 replay. Validate dedupe behavior against local ledger shim.
- Phase 2 (Core, 7 days): implement production worker in Go using existing job runner framework; integrate with Kafka topics and ledger preflight endpoint; add feature flag gating.
- Phase 3 (Validator, 5 days): implement streaming validator with Flink/Beam job atop consumption of enriched meter events; persist anomalies to anomalies.events topic and write compacted anomaly index for console queries.
- Phase 4 (Observability & rollout, 3 days): dashboards, runbooks, canary rollout to 10% of tenants, and escalation docs.

Rollout & migration steps:
1) Deploy resurfacer to staging, run with dry-run mode for a 30-day lookback. Verify no ledger writes.
2) Enable write mode against a synthetic tenant prefix. Validate ledger preflight rejects duplicates.
3) Canary: enable write mode for 50 small tenants for 48h. Monitor counts and customer-impact metric.
4) Ramp to full run for lookback window of 7 days.

Monitoring & alerts:
- Alert if resurfacer error_rate > 0.5% for 1h.
- Alert if validator anomalies per 24h exceed 0.1% of total events or >5 tenants affected.
- Dashboard panels for repair volume by cause, average time-to-detect, and post-repair audit checks.

Data retention & privacy:
- Anomaly records contain only tenant_id and non-sensitive routing attributes; personally identifiable payloads must be redacted before persistence.

Security review required: true

Dependencies:
- ledger preflight endpoint (ENG-9421-like ledger work) -> required for dedupe checks
- tenant-routing-log enrichment job (ENG-21456-ish) -> for routing history joins
- console-anomaly-index storage (new compacted table)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: resurfacer emits duplicate credits if preflight is flaky. Mitigation: implement a conservative preflight timeout and an operator lock that halts writer if preflight SLA is missed.
- Risk: validator false positives overwhelm ops. Mitigation: apply a confidence threshold and sample first 24h of anomalies to tune heuristics.
